title: Geo-claim assertion workflow and evidence collector for hosted endpoints
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Provide a robust hosted-API workflow that asserts a tenant's declared data residency (geo-claim) at request time and produces cryptographically verifiable evidence bundles for audit and legal review. The feature should support declarative tenant residency preferences (soft-claim), enforced region-locking (hard-claim), and an evidence export pipeline that packages request traces, routing decisions, storage location metadata, and retention policy snapshots into a reproducible artifact.

Why this ticket: Customers and auditors need not only that requests are routed to an appropriate region but also an auditable snapshot that proves where data was processed and stored, for a given time window. Existing residency UI supports declarations but lacks an automated evidence collector and a clear enforcement/soft-fail policy.

High-level scope:
- API-level tenant residency flags: preference, strict_lock, allowed_regions list.
- Runtime routing signal integration (smart router) to attach resolved region and fallback reason to each request trace.
- Evidence collector service that periodically or on-demand bundles traces, model variant used, storage object locations, KMS key IDs, and retention policy versions into a signed export (manifest.json + zipped payload).
- Console UI: "Export residency evidence" action per tenant + scheduled exports for compliance cycles.
- Export formats: ZIP with JSON manifest, optionally signed with our audit key and with a KMS-signed checksum for customer-supplied HSM verification.

Out of scope for initial release: deep per-token content hashing, cross-account customer-hosted attestations. Those are backlog items to evaluate after initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Tenant can set residency preference and strict_lock via API/Console and it is persisted in tenant config.
2) For requests to hosted endpoints, routing decisions include resolved_region and fallback_reason written to trace and request metadata.
3) Evidence export bundles contain: manifest.json (tenant id, time window, policy version, KMS key ids), trace archive (logs trimmed to retention-safe subset), object storage location list, and a signed checksum file.
4) Console can trigger an on-demand evidence export; exported artifact is downloadable and recorded in audit log.
5) Scheduled exports run successfully for a tenant for a 30-day window and upload to customer-designated bucket if provided.
6) Legal/Compliance has reviewed exported manifest fields and signed off on minimal dataset for compliance review.
7) Performance: enabling strict_lock must not increase p50 latency by more than 10% (measured in canary).
history: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Maya Chen — initial scoping and stakeholder list (Legal, Infra, Runtime, Console).

2025-02-13: Architecture sync with Runtime (Attendees: Liam O'Connor, Priya Singh). Decided evidence collector will fetch traces from tracing store and complement with runtime metadata rather than instrument runtime to write bulky artifacts inline. Trade-off: simpler runtime change vs increased collector complexity.
2025-02-14: Legal provided feedback — manifest must include policy version and retention snapshot; remove any PII from trace exports. Action: add trace redaction step in collector.
2025-02-16: UX sketch review (link in artifacts) — Console export flow added with tenant-level settings. Design requests: show estimated export size and retention exposure info during export.
2025-02-18: Security raised KMS concerns: customer-supplied KMS integration and key-rotation handling required for signed exports. Blocker recorded: ENG dependency on KMS integration (ENG-18234).

2025-02-20: PM/ENG alignment — scope trimmed for MVP: support platform-signed exports and optional S3 upload; customer HSM/KMS support to follow in next cycle. Updated acceptance criteria and release target.
notes:
Implementation notes: collector should be idempotent and support incremental snapshots to avoid repeated full exports. Consider content-addressable storage for trace chunks to reduce bundle size. Runtime team to add a small metadata envelope to request traces — resolved_region, route_policy_version, model_variant_id — that collector will index.

Follow-ups: 1) ENG: implement trace envelope (ENG-72190). 2) DES: UI microcopy for export modal & consent flow (DES-1451). 3) PM: schedule Compliance review session post-MVP.
